fixes.explanation: Right on, baker. The speaker says, “I, the LORD, am its keeper…” The LORD Himself holds the job. A vineyard with that keeper is in good hands.
Yes, it's false. The LORD says, “I guard it night and day…” That covers the whole clock, not just the daylight hours. When the sun goes down, the guarding goes on.
Good guess if you're picturing a game of hide and seek, friend. But the text says the LORD guards it “…so no one can disturb it…” The word the text gives is disturb. Find isn't in the verse.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, “I am not angry.” He says it right after He talks about guarding the vineyard. I think that's a surprise, because the guard is not angry at all. It comes in verse 4.

The text says the opposite, friend. The LORD says that if thorns and briers confronted Him, “…I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.” So no sharing the garden bed in that picture. Thorns and vines don't get to be neighbors here.

Moving day never comes up, baker. The LORD says, “If only thorns and briers confronted Me, I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.” Nothing in the verse has Him moving the vineyard. What He says He would do is march against them.

This plant isn't pictured staying in one field, friend. The text says Israel will “…bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.” That's about as far from hidden as it gets. The fruit reaches the whole world.

Yes, baker. The text says, “There the calves graze, and there they lie down…” The fortified city is deserted, so the calves are the ones grazing there. The city looks very different from a stronghold now.

That's what the text says, baker. “…for this is a people without understanding.” Then it says their Maker has no compassion on them and their Creator shows them no favor. Verse 11 gives that reason right alongside it.

Exactly, baker. The text says, “…you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.” The gathering is one by one, and that's the promise the text gives. It's a gathering of Israelites, and the text says it plainly.
Pairs sound neat, friend, like a buddy system. But the text says, “…you, O Israelites, will be gathered one by one.” It's one by one, not two by two. The text doesn't mention pairs.
Not quite, baker. The text says, “…those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt.” Both groups come forth. The exiles in Egypt are included.

Yes, it's false. The text says, “…those who were perishing in Assyria will come forth with those who were exiles in Egypt.” They come forth together, from both places. The exiles in Egypt are part of it.

Egypt is where some of them were exiles, baker. But the text says they “…will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.” The worship it names is in Jerusalem. No temple in Egypt appears in these verses.
